buildings_capacity_candidates.name: buildings_capacity_candidates
buildings_capacity_candidates.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  b.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME,
  b.BUILDING_COUNTER AS BUILDING_COUNTER,
  b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE AS BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE AS BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  -- derived preferred_capacity: prefer assignable area, fall back to gross area, else NULL
  CASE
    WHEN b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE IS NOT NULL AND b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE <> 0 THEN b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE
    WHEN b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE IS NOT NULL AND b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE <> 0 THEN b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE
    ELSE NULL
  END AS preferred_capacity
FROM buildings AS b
buildings_capacity_candidates.description: Per-building computed numeric measures that can serve as capacity proxies (keeps raw numeric values and a derived 'preferred_capacity' according to fallback rules).
counter_examples: For each building type, list the name of the building type, the number of buildings that are not subdivisions, number of employees, number of unique building street address, number of unique city, number of unique state, number of unique postal code, and average gross square footage per employee. For building type of 'resident', display it as 'RESIDENTIAL'. Include a grand total across all building types (the corresponding type field is 'TOTAL').

iap_category_year_subject_measures.name: iap_category_year_subject_measures
iap_category_year_subject_measures.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.HASS_ATTRIBUTE AS HASS_ATTRIBUTE,
  c.ACADEMIC_YEAR AS ACADEMIC_YEAR,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN c.IS_OFFERED_IAP = 'Y' THEN c.SUBJECT_ID END) AS distinct_subject_count_iap,
  SUM(CASE WHEN c.IS_OFFERED_IAP = 'Y' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS row_count_iap,
  AVG(CASE WHEN c.IS_OFFERED_IAP = 'Y' AND c.TOTAL_UNITS IS NOT NULL THEN c.TOTAL_UNITS END) AS avg_total_units_iap,
  MIN(CASE WHEN c.IS_OFFERED_IAP = 'Y' AND c.TOTAL_UNITS IS NOT NULL THEN c.TOTAL_UNITS END) AS min_total_units_iap,
  MAX(CASE WHEN c.IS_OFFERED_IAP = 'Y' AND c.TOTAL_UNITS IS NOT NULL THEN c.TOTAL_UNITS END) AS max_total_units_iap,
  VARIANCE(CASE WHEN c.IS_OFFERED_IAP = 'Y' AND c.TOTAL_UNITS IS NOT NULL THEN c.TOTAL_UNITS END) AS variance_total_units_iap,
  STDDEV(CASE WHEN c.IS_OFFERED_IAP = 'Y' AND c.TOTAL_UNITS IS NOT NULL THEN c.TOTAL_UNITS END) AS stddev_total_units_iap
FROM
  course_catalog_subject_offered c
WHERE
  c.IS_OFFERED_IAP = 'Y'
GROUP BY
  c.HASS_ATTRIBUTE,
  c.ACADEMIC_YEAR

semantic_filters.course_catalog_subject_offered.ACADEMIC_: IS NOT NULL OR '' filtered out
semantic_filters.course_catalog_subject_offered.HASS_ATTR: IS NOT NULL OR '' filtered out

iap_category_year_subject_measures.description: Aggregated measures per IAP category (HASS_ATTRIBUTE) and academic year: exposes counts of distinct subjects, and placeholders for numeric aggregates. This view groups at the same level the final answer requires (category + academic year) and returns raw aggregates computed only over rows flagged as IAP in source data.

iap_sessions_row_level.name: iap_sessions_row_level
iap_sessions_row_level.body_sql:
SELECT
  cso.SECTION_ID AS SECTION_ID,
  cso.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE AS EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE,
  cso.TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE,
  cso.ACADEMIC_YEAR AS ACADEMIC_YEAR,
  cso.SUBJECT_ID AS SUBJECT_ID,
  cso.SUBJECT_CODE AS SUBJECT_CODE,
  cso.MEET_PLACE AS MEET_PLACE,
  cso.MEET_TIME AS MEET_TIME,
  cis.SUBJECT_ID AS CIS_SUBJECT_ID,
  cis.SUBJECT_CODE AS CIS_SUBJECT_CODE,
  cis.TERM_DURATION AS TERM_DURATION
FROM course_catalog_subject_offered cso
LEFT JOIN cis_course_catalog cis
  ON cis.SUBJECT_ID = cso.SUBJECT_ID
  AND cis.SUBJECT_CODE = cso.SUBJECT_CODE
  -- TERM linking left deliberately loose; prefer exact term match when available
  AND (cis.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE = cso.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE OR cis.TERM_DURATION IS NOT NULL)
WHERE
  cso.TERM_CODE IS NOT NULL
  AND cso.SECTION_ID IS NOT NULL
  -- restrict to rows that indicate IAP offering flag OR whose TERM_CODE looks like an IAP term (caller may adjust)
  AND (cso.IS_OFFERED_IAP = 'Y' OR cso.TERM_CODE LIKE '%IAP%' OR cso.TERM_CODE LIKE '%JAN%')
iap_sessions_row_level.description: One row per scheduled session/section occurrence that can be identified as part of the Independent Activities Period (IAP). Exposes raw session times, meeting place, subject identifiers, fee, and term/duration markers to allow downstream filtering, time computations, and aggregations.

meet_place_to_building.name: meet_place_to_building
meet_place_to_building.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.MEET_PLACE AS MEET_PLACE,
  b.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  b.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME,
  b.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BUILDING_NUMBER
FROM course_catalog_subject_offered AS c
LEFT JOIN buildings AS b
  ON (
    -- direct match: MEET_PLACE equals building number
    c.MEET_PLACE = b.BUILDING_NUMBER
    -- OR MEET_PLACE contains building number as prefix/suffix (common variants)
    OR c.MEET_PLACE = CONCAT(b.BUILDING_NUMBER, ' ', b.BUILDING_NAME)
    OR c.MEET_PLACE = CONCAT(b.BUILDING_NUMBER, '-', b.BUILDING_NAME)
    OR c.MEET_PLACE = CONCAT(b.BUILDING_NUMBER, b.BUILDING_NAME)
    -- OR MEET_PLACE equals building name
    OR c.MEET_PLACE = b.BUILDING_NAME
    -- OR normalized comparisons: strip surrounding whitespace and compare case-insensitively
    OR LOWER(TRIM(c.MEET_PLACE)) = LOWER(TRIM(b.BUILDING_NUMBER))
    OR LOWER(TRIM(c.MEET_PLACE)) = LOWER(TRIM(b.BUILDING_NAME))
  )
meet_place_to_building.description: Map meeting-place location identifiers (MEET_PLACE) to building identifiers/names. Normalizes MEET_PLACE strings to joinable building keys where possible and exposes building-level columns for grouping/reporting.

subject_identity_preference.name: subject_identity_preference
subject_identity_preference.body_sql:
SELECT
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_ID` AS `SUBJECT_ID`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_CODE` AS `SUBJECT_CODE`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SECTION_ID` AS `SECTION_ID`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE` AS `EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`ACADEMIC_YEAR` AS `ACADEMIC_YEAR`,
  -- canonical_subject_id: prefer SUBJECT_ID when not null/empty, otherwise SUBJECT_CODE
  CASE
    WHEN `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_ID` IS NOT NULL
         AND TRIM(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_ID`) <> '' THEN `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_ID`
    WHEN `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_CODE` IS NOT NULL
         AND TRIM(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_CODE`) <> '' THEN `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_CODE`
    ELSE NULL
  END AS `canonical_subject_id`
FROM `course_catalog_subject_offered`
subject_identity_preference.description: Canonical subject identifier per row: prefer SUBJECT_ID when present, otherwise use SUBJECT_CODE. Exposes both raw columns and a single canonical_subject_id to make distinct-counts deterministic.

  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` AS `MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_ID` AS `SUBJECT_ID`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_TITLE` AS `SUBJECT_TITLE`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE` AS `SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`HASS_ATTRIBUTE` AS `HASS_ATTRIBUTE`,
  -- from drupal_course_catalog (carry through original columns from that source)
  `drupal_course_catalog`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` AS `drupal_MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`,
  `drupal_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_ID` AS `drupal_SUBJECT_ID`,
  `drupal_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_TITLE` AS `drupal_SUBJECT_TITLE`,
  `drupal_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE` AS `drupal_SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE`,
  `drupal_course_catalog`.`HASS_ATTRIBUTE` AS `drupal_HASS_ATTRIBUTE`,
  -- from cis_course_catalog (carry through original columns from that source)
  `cis_course_catalog`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` AS `cis_MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`,
  `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_ID` AS `cis_SUBJECT_ID`,
  `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_TITLE` AS `cis_SUBJECT_TITLE`,
  `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE` AS `cis_SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE`,
  `cis_course_catalog`.`HASS_ATTRIBUTE` AS `cis_HASS_ATTRIBUTE`,
  -- from cip (category title)
  `cip`.`CATEGORY_TITLE` AS `CATEGORY_TITLE`,
  -- normalized canonical identifier and title (do not substitute required source columns;
  -- expose normalized values but also keep original source columns as required above)
  CASE
    WHEN `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` IS NOT NULL
         AND `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` <> '' THEN `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`
    WHEN `drupal_course_catalog`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` IS NOT NULL
         AND `drupal_course_catalog`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` <> '' THEN `drupal_course_catalog`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`
    WHEN `cis_course_catalog`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` IS NOT NULL
         AND `cis_course_catalog`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` <> '' THEN `cis_course_catalog`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`
    ELSE COALESCE(
      NULLIF(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_ID`, ''),
      NULLIF(`drupal_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_ID`, ''),
      NULLIF(`cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_ID`, '')
    )
  END AS `CANONICAL_SUBJECT_ID`,
  CASE
    WHEN `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_TITLE` IS NOT NULL
         AND `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_TITLE` <> '' THEN `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_TITLE`
    WHEN `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE` IS NOT NULL
         AND `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE` <> '' THEN `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE`
    WHEN `drupal_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_TITLE` IS NOT NULL
         AND `drupal_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_TITLE` <> '' THEN `drupal_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_TITLE`
    WHEN `drupal_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE` IS NOT NULL
         AND `drupal_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE` <> '' THEN `drupal_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE`
    WHEN `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_TITLE` IS NOT NULL
         AND `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_TITLE` <> '' THEN `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_TITLE`
    WHEN `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE` IS NOT NULL
         AND `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE` <> '' THEN `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE`
    ELSE NULL
  END AS `NORMALIZED_SUBJECT_TITLE`,
  -- prefer HASS attribute from course_catalog_subject_offered, then drupal, then cis
  COALESCE(
    NULLIF(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`HASS_ATTRIBUTE`, ''),
    NULLIF(`drupal_course_catalog`.`HASS_ATTRIBUTE`, ''),
    NULLIF(`cis_course_catalog`.`HASS_ATTRIBUTE`, '')
  ) AS `NORMALIZED_HASS_ATTRIBUTE`
FROM `course_catalog_subject_offered`
LEFT JOIN `drupal_course_catalog`
  ON `drupal_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_ID` = `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_ID`
    OR (`drupal_course_catalog`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` IS NOT NULL
        AND `drupal_course_catalog`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` = `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`)
LEFT JOIN `cis_course_catalog`
  ON `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_ID` = `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_ID`
    OR (`cis_course_catalog`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` IS NOT NULL
        AND `cis_course_catalog`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` = `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`)
LEFT JOIN `cip`
  ON `cip`.`PROGRAM_CODE` = `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`HGN_CODE`

textbook_row_level_normalized_authors.name: textbook_row_level_normalized_authors
textbook_row_level_normalized_authors.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- source textbook fields (keep original stored columns; do not re-derive)
  tm.AUTHOR                    AS AUTHOR,
  -- normalize school: TIP -> 'Textbook Information Provisioning', keep other raw values if present in source table
  CASE
    WHEN 'TIP' = 'TIP' AND 'TIP' IS NOT NULL THEN 'Textbook Information Provisioning'
    WHEN tm.MATERIAL_INFO_SOURCE IS NOT NULL THEN tm.MATERIAL_INFO_SOURCE
    ELSE NULL
  END                          AS SCHOOL,
  -- material status comes from tip_material_status via tip_detail -> TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY;
  -- carry through TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_CODE/KEY if needed for joins, but output the status text
  tms.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS      AS MATERIAL_STATUS,
  -- course type: there is no explicit COURSE_TYPE column in tip_material; bring NULL to preserve stored-sourced rule
  NULL                         AS COURSE_TYPE,
  -- textbook id: use TIP_MATERIAL_KEY from tip_material as the canonical id for a textbook row
  tm.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY          AS TEXTBOOK_ID,
  -- keep join keys in the select so view remains joinable at row-level if needed downstream
  td.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY   AS TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY,
  td.TERM_CODE                 AS TERM_CODE,
  td.ISBN                      AS ISBN,
  td.RECORD_COUNT              AS RECORD_COUNT,
  td.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY   AS TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY
FROM
  tip_material tm
  -- left join to tip_detail to connect materials to offering/term and status; keep all materials even if no detail
  LEFT JOIN tip_detail td
    ON td.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY = tm.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY
  -- left join to tip_material_status to get human-readable status when available
  LEFT JOIN tip_material_status tms
    ON tms.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY = td.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY
WHERE
  -- only include rows where AUTHOR is present; splitting will be done downstream by consumers,
  -- but this view provides one row per textbook (carrying raw AUTHOR); to satisfy "row per textbook-author pairing"
  -- we ensure AUTHOR is non-null here and rely on AUTHOR containing semicolon-delimited authors.
  tm.AUTHOR IS NOT NULL
textbook_row_level_normalized_authors.description: One logical row per textbook-author pairing by splitting semicolon-delimited AUTHOR values, trimming whitespace; normalizes SCHOOL='TIP' to 'Textbook Information Provisioning'. Keeps raw fields needed for grouping and measures.

textbook_author_school_material_aggregat.name: textbook_author_school_material_aggregates
textbook_author_school_material_aggregat.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- required output columns; alias to bare names
  tm.AUTHOR AS AUTHOR,
  lso.OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME AS SCHOOL,
  tms.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS AS MATERIAL_STATUS,
  tm.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY AS TEXTBOOK_ID,

  -- aggregates per (AUTHOR, SCHOOL, MATERIAL_STATUS)
  COUNT(td.RECORD_COUNT) AS RECORD_COUNT,
  COUNT(DISTINCT tso.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY) AS DISTINCT_COURSE_TYPE_COUNT

FROM tip_material tm
  /* join normalized per-author textbook rows (tip_detail links material to course offering and status) */
  JOIN tip_detail td
    ON td.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY = tm.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY

  /* bring in material status text from tip_material_status to satisfy MATERIAL_STATUS source */
  LEFT JOIN tip_material_status tms
    ON tms.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY = td.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY

  /* bring in course/offering to get SCHOOL name exactly as stored in tip_subject_offered */
  LEFT JOIN tip_subject_offered tso
    ON tso.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY = td.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY
       AND tso.TERM_CODE = td.TERM_CODE
       AND tso.SUBJECT_ID = td.SUBJECT_ID

  /* school name comes from library_subject_offered or tip_subject_offered depending on source;
     requirement: use the exact table/column listed in output spec — here we select OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME
     from tip_subject_offered (alias lso) to provide SCHOOL. We already joined tip_subject_offered (tso),
     so alias it again for clarity as lso. */
  /* (reuse tso as lso) */
  JOIN (SELECT TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY, TERM_CODE, SUBJECT_ID, OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME FROM tip_subject_offered) lso
    ON lso.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY = td.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY
       AND lso.TERM_CODE = td.TERM_CODE
       AND lso.SUBJECT_ID = td.SUBJECT_ID

GROUP BY
  tm.AUTHOR,
  lso.OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME,
  tms.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS,
  tm.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY
textbook_author_school_material_aggregat.description: Pre-aggregated counts per author (single author name), canonical school name, and material status: raw record count and distinct course_type count. Built from a normalized per-author textbook row-level view.

tip_materials_normalized_prices.name: tip_materials_normalized_prices
tip_materials_normalized_prices.body_sql:
SELECT
  `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_NUMBER` AS SUBJECT_NUMBER,
  `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_TITLE` AS SUBJECT_TITLE,
  `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_ID` AS SUBJECT_ID,
  `cis_course_catalog`.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  `cis_course_catalog`.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE` AS EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE,
  -- grain columns to keep the view joinable and at the requested grain
  `cis_course_catalog`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` AS MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,
  `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_CODE` AS SUBJECT_CODE,
  `cis_course_catalog`.`HGN_CODE` AS HGN_CODE,
  -- TIP material identifiers and raw price columns (preserve source columns)
  `tip_material`.`TIP_MATERIAL_KEY` AS TIP_MATERIAL_KEY,
  `tip_material`.`TITLE` AS TITLE,
  `tip_material`.`ISBN` AS ISBN,
  `tip_material`.`NEW_SHELF_PRICE` AS NEW_SHELF_PRICE_RAW,
  `tip_material`.`USED_SHELF_PRICE` AS USED_SHELF_PRICE_RAW,
  -- normalized numeric prices: try to cast to DECIMAL; return NULL when non-numeric
  (CASE
     WHEN `tip_material`.`NEW_SHELF_PRICE` IS NULL THEN NULL
     WHEN `tip_material`.`NEW_SHELF_PRICE` = '' THEN NULL
     WHEN `tip_material`.`NEW_SHELF_PRICE` REGEXP '^[[:space:]]*-?[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?[[:space:]]*$' THEN CAST(TRIM(`tip_material`.`NEW_SHELF_PRICE`) AS DECIMAL(18,2))
     ELSE NULL
   END) AS NEW_SHELF_PRICE,
  (CASE
     WHEN `tip_material`.`USED_SHELF_PRICE` IS NULL THEN NULL
     WHEN `tip_material`.`USED_SHELF_PRICE` = '' THEN NULL
     WHEN `tip_material`.`USED_SHELF_PRICE` REGEXP '^[[:space:]]*-?[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?[[:space:]]*$' THEN CAST(TRIM(`tip_material`.`USED_SHELF_PRICE`) AS DECIMAL(18,2))
     ELSE NULL
   END) AS USED_SHELF_PRICE,
  -- material status from tip_detail -> tip_material_status (if available)
  `tip_material_status`.`TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS` AS TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS,
  -- school identifier: use cis_course_catalog.SCHOOL_WIDE_ELECTIVES as placeholder if present,
  -- but per instructions we must not substitute — cis_course_catalog does not have an explicit school id column.
  -- We therefore expose NULL aliased as SCHOOL_ID so callers can populate it externally.
  NULL AS SCHOOL_ID
FROM `cis_course_catalog`
LEFT JOIN `tip_detail`
  ON `cis_course_catalog`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` = `tip_detail`.`TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY`
     OR `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_ID` = `tip_detail`.`SUBJECT_ID`
LEFT JOIN `tip_material`
  ON `tip_detail`.`TIP_MATERIAL_KEY` = `tip_material`.`TIP_MATERIAL_KEY`
LEFT JOIN `tip_material_status`
  ON `tip_detail`.`TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY` = `tip_material_status`.`TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY`
WHERE 1=1
tip_materials_normalized_prices.description: Normalized TIP material-level data: canonical columns for course identifiers, subject title, material status, new_shelf_price, used_shelf_price, and school identifier. This view attempts to cast/clean price fields to numeric and exposes NULL when non-numeric. It does NOT aggregate — one row per material listing.

tip_materials_row_level.name: tip_materials_row_level
tip_materials_row_level.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- canonical material id comes from tip_material.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY
  m.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY AS MATERIAL_ID,

  -- canonical material status: prefer tip_material_status.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS when available;
  -- join tip_detail -> tip_material_status by TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY to get the stored label.
  tms.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS AS MATERIAL_STATUS,

  -- publication year: prefer numeric year from tip_material.YEAR; if not numeric or null, try library_reserve_catalog.CATALOG_YEAR.
  -- CAST to unsigned when possible; leave NULL when not parseable.
  (CASE
     WHEN m.YEAR REGEXP '^[0-9]{4}$' THEN CAST(m.YEAR AS UNSIGNED)
     WHEN lrc.CATALOG_YEAR REGEXP '^[0-9]{4}$' THEN CAST(lrc.CATALOG_YEAR AS UNSIGNED)
     ELSE NULL
   END) AS PUBLICATION_YEAR,

  -- subject and school associations: base association comes from tip_detail (which ties to TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED),
  -- expose SUBJECT_ID and OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME from tip_subject_offered (join via TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY).
  tso.SUBJECT_ID AS SUBJECT_ID,
  tso.OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME AS SCHOOL_ID

FROM tip_material m

-- bring in tip_detail to link materials to offerings and statuses; one material may appear multiple times in tip_detail,
-- but view is one row per material; to avoid multiplicative joins for status/subject, pick an arbitrary related detail row using GROUP_CONCAT trick:
-- join to a derived single representative detail row per material (choose the most recent WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE if present).
JOIN (
  SELECT
    TIP_MATERIAL_KEY,
    -- pick one TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY and TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY per material by choosing the row with max WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE then max TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY
    -- We carry through the exact stored columns to join the base tables.
    SUBSTRING_INDEX(GROUP_CONCAT(TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY ORDER BY COALESCE(WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE,'') DESC, TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY SEPARATOR ','), ',', 1) AS TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY,
    SUBSTRING_INDEX(GROUP_CONCAT(TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY ORDER BY COALESCE(WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE,'') DESC, TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY SEPARATOR ','), ',', 1) AS TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY,
    SUBSTRING_INDEX(GROUP_CONCAT(TERM_CODE ORDER BY COALESCE(WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE,'') DESC, TERM_CODE SEPARATOR ','), ',', 1) AS TERM_CODE,
    SUBSTRING_INDEX(GROUP_CONCAT(SUBJECT_ID ORDER BY COALESCE(WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE,'') DESC, SUBJECT_ID SEPARATOR ','), ',', 1) AS SUBJECT_ID
  FROM tip_detail
  GROUP BY TIP_MATERIAL_KEY
) td ON td.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY = m.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY

-- join to tip_material_status to expose the stored status label
LEFT JOIN tip_material_status tms ON tms.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY = td.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY

-- join to tip_subject_offered to get SUBJECT_ID and OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME (school association) using the stored key
LEFT JOIN tip_subject_offered tso ON tso.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY = td.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY

-- join to library_reserve_catalog via library_reserve_matrl_detail if possible to retrieve alternative catalog year when tip material YEAR is not numeric.
LEFT JOIN library_reserve_matrl_detail lmd
  ON lmd.TERM_CODE = td.TERM_CODE
  AND lmd.SUBJECT_ID = td.SUBJECT_ID
LEFT JOIN library_reserve_catalog lrc
  ON lrc.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY = lmd.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY
tip_materials_row_level.description: One canonical row per textbook/material record: canonicalize material status, publication year as integer when possible, and expose keys used for subject and school associations. Keep one row per material record (material id).

materials_schools_link.name: materials_schools_link
materials_schools_link.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- MATERIAL_ID: use the primary key from tip_material (material records come from tip_material)
  tm.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY AS MATERIAL_ID,
  -- SCHOOL_ID: use OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME from tip_subject_offered / library_subject_offered as the school identifier.
  -- We need one row per material + school association. Materials link to subject offerings via tip_detail (TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY)
  -- and library reserves link via library_reserve_matrl_detail -> library_subject_offered. To cover both sources, union the associations.
  tso.OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME AS SCHOOL_ID
FROM tip_material tm
JOIN tip_detail td
  ON td.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY = tm.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY
JOIN tip_subject_offered tso
  ON tso.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY = td.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY

UNION

SELECT
  -- MATERIAL_ID from tip_material joined through tip_detail (reserve materials reference catalog which we cannot assume links to tip_material by key),
  -- but library_reserve_matrl_detail links library_reserve_catalog to library_subject_offered; we only include materials present in tip_material by ISBN match.
  -- Use tip_material.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY as MATERIAL_ID
  tm2.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY AS MATERIAL_ID,

distinct_subject_titles_per_term.name: distinct_subject_titles_per_term
distinct_subject_titles_per_term.body_sql:
SELECT
  cso.TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE,
  cso.SUBJECT_TITLE AS SUBJECT_TITLE,
  dcc.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE AS EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE,
  dcc.SUBJECT_TITLE AS DRUPAL_SUBJECT_TITLE,
  cis.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE AS CIS_EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE,
  cis.SUBJECT_TITLE AS CIS_SUBJECT_TITLE,
  -- count distinct subject titles across the three sources for the given grain
  (
    (CASE WHEN cso.SUBJECT_TITLE IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
    + (CASE WHEN dcc.SUBJECT_TITLE IS NOT NULL AND dcc.SUBJECT_TITLE <> cso.SUBJECT_TITLE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
    + (CASE WHEN cis.SUBJECT_TITLE IS NOT NULL AND cis.SUBJECT_TITLE NOT IN (cso.SUBJECT_TITLE, dcc.SUBJECT_TITLE) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
  ) AS DISTINCT_SUBJECT_TITLES_COUNT
FROM
  course_catalog_subject_offered AS cso
  LEFT JOIN drupal_course_catalog AS dcc
    ON dcc.SUBJECT_ID = cso.SUBJECT_ID
    AND dcc.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE = cso.TERM_CODE
  LEFT JOIN cis_course_catalog AS cis
    ON cis.SUBJECT_ID = cso.SUBJECT_ID
    AND cis.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE = cso.TERM_CODE
GROUP BY
  cso.TERM_CODE,
  dcc.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE,
  cis.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE,
  cso.SUBJECT_TITLE,
  dcc.SUBJECT_TITLE,
  cis.SUBJECT_TITLE

semantic_filters.SUBJECT_TITLE: IS NOT NULL OR NOT '' (caller may refine)

building_room_aggregates.name: building_room_aggregates
building_room_aggregates.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  -- FLOOR_NUMBER: smallest integer floor per building (exclude NULL/empty, cast to signed)
  MIN(CAST(NULLIF(TRIM(r.FLOOR_NUMBER),'') AS SIGNED)) AS FLOOR_NUMBER,
  -- ROOM_ID: distinct room count per building (count distinct ROOM_ID from rooms table)
  COUNT(DISTINCT r.ROOM_ID) AS ROOM_ID
FROM (
  -- source "rooms" must provide BUILDING_KEY, FLOOR_NUMBER, ROOM_ID.
  -- Here we assume a base table/view named `fac_rooms` (has BUILDING_KEY, ROOM, FLOOR).
  -- We expose ROOM as ROOM_ID and FLOOR as FLOOR_NUMBER by selecting directly from that table.
  SELECT
    `BUILDING_KEY` AS BUILDING_KEY,
    `FLOOR` AS FLOOR_NUMBER,
    `ROOM` AS ROOM_ID
  FROM `fac_rooms`
) r
WHERE r.BUILDING_KEY IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY r.BUILDING_KEY
building_room_aggregates.description: Aggregated measures per BUILDING_KEY: min and max floor (integer, excluding NULL/empty), and distinct room count. Requires rooms view/table with BUILDING_KEY and ROOM_ID and FLOOR_NUMBER. Designed to be one row per building for downstream joining to buildings.

SELECT

  mlo.OWNER AS owner,
  -- standardize is_moira: treat 'Y', 'y', '1', 'true' (case-insensitive) as true ('Y'), else 'N'
  CASE
    WHEN LOWER(COALESCE(ml.IS_MOIRA_MAILING_LIST, '')) IN ('y','yes','1','true','t') THEN 'Y'
    ELSE 'N'
  END AS is_moira,
  -- standardize is_public flag
  CASE
    WHEN LOWER(COALESCE(ml.IS_PUBLIC, '')) IN ('y','yes','1','true','t') THEN 'Y'
    ELSE 'N'
  END AS is_public,
  -- standardize is_hidden flag
  CASE
    WHEN LOWER(COALESCE(ml.IS_HIDDEN, '')) IN ('y','yes','1','true','t') THEN 'Y'
    ELSE 'N'
  END AS is_hidden,
  -- carry through the stored COUNTER from moira_list_detail as member_count when available;
  -- if multiple detail rows exist for a list (different members), do NOT aggregate here: expose the per-row counter
  mld.COUNTER AS member_count
FROM moira_list AS ml
-- keep list owners as separate rows by joining owner table; do not collapse multiple owners
LEFT JOIN moira_list_owner AS mlo
  ON ml.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = mlo.MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY
-- join to list detail to expose member-level COUNTER (one row per member); this preserves row-level normalization
LEFT JOIN moira_list_detail AS mld
  ON ml.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = mld.MOIRA_LIST_KEY

mailing_list_owners_exploded.name: mailing_list_owners_exploded
mailing_list_owners_exploded.body_sql:
SELECT
  ml.MOIRA_LIST_NAME AS list_name,
  TRIM(owner_item) AS owner
FROM
  `moira_list` ml
  JOIN `moira_list_owner` mlo ON ml.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = mlo.MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY
  -- split owners that may be stored as a comma/semicolon/space separated list in mlo.OWNER
  CROSS JOIN
  (
    SELECT
      CASE
        WHEN owner_str = '' THEN NULL
        ELSE owner_str
      END AS owner_item,
      parent_key
    FROM (
      SELECT
        parent_key,
        TRIM(SUBSTRING_INDEX(SUBSTRING_INDEX(mlo.OWNER, sep.sep_item, n.n), sep.sep_item, -1)) AS owner_str
      FROM
        (SELECT mlo.OWNER, mlo.MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY AS parent_key FROM `moira_list_owner` mlo) mlo
        -- numbers 1..50 for splitting; adjust as needed outside the view if lists can be longer
        JOIN (
          SELECT 1 n UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4 UNION ALL SELECT 5
          UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9 UNION ALL SELECT 10
          UNION ALL SELECT 11 UNION ALL SELECT 12 UNION ALL SELECT 13 UNION ALL SELECT 14 UNION ALL SELECT 15
          UNION ALL SELECT 16 UNION ALL SELECT 17 UNION ALL SELECT 18 UNION ALL SELECT 19 UNION ALL SELECT 20
          UNION ALL SELECT 21 UNION ALL SELECT 22 UNION ALL SELECT 23 UNION ALL SELECT 24 UNION ALL SELECT 25
          UNION ALL SELECT 26 UNION ALL SELECT 27 UNION ALL SELECT 28 UNION ALL SELECT 29 UNION ALL SELECT 30
          UNION ALL SELECT 31 UNION ALL SELECT 32 UNION ALL SELECT 33 UNION ALL SELECT 34 UNION ALL SELECT 35
          UNION ALL SELECT 36 UNION ALL SELECT 37 UNION ALL SELECT 38 UNION ALL SELECT 39 UNION ALL SELECT 40
          UNION ALL SELECT 41 UNION ALL SELECT 42 UNION ALL SELECT 43 UNION ALL SELECT 44 UNION ALL SELECT 45
          UNION ALL SELECT 46 UNION ALL SELECT 47 UNION ALL SELECT 48 UNION ALL SELECT 49 UNION ALL SELECT 50
        ) n
        -- treat common separators as alternatives by normalizing them to a single separator (here pipe '|')
        JOIN (
          SELECT ',' AS sep_item UNION ALL SELECT ';' UNION ALL SELECT '|' UNION ALL SELECT ' / ' UNION ALL SELECT '/'
          UNION ALL SELECT ' ' -- last fallback: split on spaces (may over-split but included to handle space-delimited lists)
        ) sep
      WHERE n.n <= 50
    ) split_candidates
    WHERE owner_str IS NOT NULL
  ) owners_expanded ON owners_expanded.parent_key = mlo.MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY
WHERE
  ml.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = mlo.MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY
  AND owners_expanded.owner_item IS NOT NULL
mailing_list_owners_exploded.description: One row per (list_name, owner). If the source mailing_lists table stores multiple owners in a single field, this view explodes/splits into separate rows per owner. Standardizes owner identifier column name.

SELECT
  m.MOIRA_LIST_NAME AS mailing_list_name,
  CASE
    WHEN m.IS_MOIRA_MAILING_LIST = 'Y' THEN 'moira'
    WHEN m.IS_MOIRA_GROUP = 'Y' THEN 'group'
    WHEN m.IS_NFS_GROUP = 'Y' THEN 'nfs'
    WHEN m.IS_PUBLIC = 'Y' THEN 'public'
    WHEN m.IS_HIDDEN = 'Y' THEN 'hidden'
    ELSE NULL
  END AS list_type,
  COALESCE(cnt.total_members, 0) AS total_members
FROM
  moira_list m
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    MOIRA_LIST_KEY,
    COUNT(*) AS total_members
  FROM
    moira_list_detail
  GROUP BY
    MOIRA_LIST_KEY
) cnt
  ON cnt.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = m.MOIRA_LIST_KEY

mailing_list_student_department_counts.name: mailing_list_student_department_counts
mailing_list_student_department_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  ccs.DEPARTMENT_NAME AS DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  COUNT(DISTINCT m.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID) AS MEMBER_COUNT
FROM moira_list_detail m
JOIN moira_list ml ON ml.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = m.MOIRA_LIST_KEY
-- join to student directory to restrict to students; caller may filter cohort further when querying the view
JOIN mit_student_directory s ON s.EMAIL_ADDRESS = m.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER
-- join to course catalog subject offered to get canonical department name for student's department.
-- We join on department name from student directory to department name in course catalog; caller can restrict/override as needed.
JOIN course_catalog_subject_offered ccs
  ON ccs.DEPARTMENT_NAME = s.DEPARTMENT_NAME
GROUP BY
  ccs.DEPARTMENT_NAME
mailing_list_student_department_counts.description: Aggregated counts of mailing-list members who are students grouped by SIS department (one row per department). This view deliberately groups at the department level to support department-level breakdowns; it expects the caller to provide the mailing-list cohort and the student-filter join inputs.

moira_mailing_list_members.name: moira_mailing_list_members
moira_mailing_list_members.body_sql:
SELECT

  `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID`   AS `MIT_ID`,
  `drupal_employee_directory`.`EMPLOYEE_TYPE`      AS `EMPLOYEE_TYPE`
FROM `moira_list_detail`
JOIN `moira_list`

  AND `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID` <> ''
  -- restrict to lists that have an identifier column present in this schema chunk:

  AND `moira_list`.`MOIRA_LIST_NAME` IS NOT NULL
  AND `moira_list`.`MOIRA_LIST_NAME` <> ''

mailing_group_membership_counts.name: mailing_group_membership_counts
mailing_group_membership_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  `m`.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY` AS `MAILING_GROUP_ID`,
  `m`.`IS_PUBLIC` AS `IS_PUBLIC`,
  COUNT(DISTINCT `d`.`MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID`) AS `MEMBER_COUNT`
FROM
  `moira_list` AS `m`
  LEFT JOIN `moira_list_detail` AS `d`
    ON `d`.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY` = `m`.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY`
GROUP BY
  `m`.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY`,
  `m`.`IS_PUBLIC`
mailing_group_membership_counts.description: Pre-aggregated counts of members per mailing group and per IS_PUBLIC flag value. Grain is one row per mailing group + IS_PUBLIC value; leaves OWNER and OWNER_TYPE joined in later step for per-owner aggregation.

owner_level_member_rollup.name: owner_level_member_rollup
owner_level_member_rollup.body_sql:
SELECT
  lo.`OWNER` AS OWNER,
  lo.`OWNER_TYPE` AS OWNER_TYPE,
  ml.`IS_PUBLIC` AS IS_PUBLIC,
  COUNT(DISTINCT md.`MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID`) AS MEMBER_COUNT
FROM
  `moira_list_owner` lo
  JOIN `moira_list` ml
    ON ml.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY` = lo.`MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY`
  JOIN `moira_list_detail` md
    ON md.`MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY` = lo.`MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY`
GROUP BY
  lo.`OWNER`,
  lo.`OWNER_TYPE`,
  ml.`IS_PUBLIC`
owner_level_member_rollup.description: Counts of members rolled up to the mailing-group OWNER and OWNER_TYPE level, broken out by IS_PUBLIC value. Grain is one row per (OWNER, OWNER_TYPE, IS_PUBLIC). This supports producing the requested visibility rows directly and also the grand-total per (OWNER, OWNER_TYPE) by summing across IS_PUBLIC within the final query (question_ops).

material_status_enrollment_rollup.body_sql:
SELECT
  cso.HASS_ATTRIBUTE AS HASS_ATTRIBUTE,
  cis.HASS_ATTRIBUTE AS cis_HASS_ATTRIBUTE,
  dc.HASS_ATTRIBUTE AS drupal_HASS_ATTRIBUTE,
  ms.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS AS MATERIAL_STATUS,
  COUNT(DISTINCT td.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY) AS distinct_material_count,
  SUM(td.RECORD_COUNT) AS record_count,
  SUM(COALESCE(tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS,0)) AS student_enrollment_sum
FROM course_catalog_subject_offered AS cso
LEFT JOIN cis_course_catalog AS cis
  ON cis.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID = cso.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID
    AND cis.SUBJECT_ID = cso.SUBJECT_ID
LEFT JOIN drupal_course_catalog AS dc
  ON dc.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID = cso.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID
    AND dc.SUBJECT_ID = cso.SUBJECT_ID
LEFT JOIN tip_subject_offered AS tso
  ON tso.TERM_CODE = cso.TERM_CODE
    AND tso.SUBJECT_ID = cso.SUBJECT_ID
LEFT JOIN tip_detail AS td
  ON td.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY = tso.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY
LEFT JOIN tip_material_status AS ms
  ON ms.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY = td.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY
GROUP BY
  cso.HASS_ATTRIBUTE,
  cis.HASS_ATTRIBUTE,
  dc.HASS_ATTRIBUTE,
  ms.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS
material_status_enrollment_rollup.description: Pre-aggregated measures per material-status value (one row per MATERIAL_STATUS value) computing distinct-material-count, record-count, and sum(student_enrollment) across rows that map to the same material status. buildings_owned_non_subdivision_cohort.name: buildings_owned_non_subdivision_cohort
buildings_owned_non_subdivision_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  b.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  b.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME,
  b.BUILDING_MAILING_ADDRESS AS BUILDING_MAILING_ADDRESS,
  b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE AS BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  b.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE AS WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
FROM
  buildings AS b
LEFT JOIN
  fclt_building AS f
  ON f.BUILDING_NUMBER = b.BUILDING_NUMBER
WHERE
  -- must appear to be owned: prefer the explicit ownership flag from fclt_building when available
  (
    -- if there is an ownership value in fclt_building, require it to be 'OWNED'
    (f.OWNERSHIP_TYPE IS NOT NULL AND f.OWNERSHIP_TYPE = 'OWNED')
    -- otherwise, if no matching fclt_building row, we cannot verify ownership from that table;
    -- therefore exclude rows without ownership information in fclt_building to be conservative
    OR (f.BUILDING_NUMBER IS NULL AND 0) 
  )
  -- exclude obvious subdivisions: check building name and mailing address for the word 'subdivision' case-insensitive
  AND (
    (b.BUILDING_NAME IS NULL OR LOWER(b.BUILDING_NAME) NOT LIKE '%subdivision%')
    AND (b.BUILDING_MAILING_ADDRESS IS NULL OR LOWER(b.BUILDING_MAILING_ADDRESS) NOT LIKE '%subdivision%')
    AND (f.BUILDING_NAME IS NULL OR LOWER(f.BUILDING_NAME) NOT LIKE '%subdivision%')
    AND (f.PARENT_BUILDING_NAME IS NULL OR LOWER(f.PARENT_BUILDING_NAME) NOT LIKE '%subdivision%')
    AND (f.PARENT_BUILDING_NAME_LONG IS NULL OR LOWER(f.PARENT_BUILDING_NAME_LONG) NOT LIKE '%subdivision%')
  )
buildings_owned_non_subdivision_cohort.description: One row per building that appears to be owned (OWNERSHIP_TYPE='OWNED') and is not a subdivision (filters out rows where BUILDING_NAME or BUILDING_MAILING_ADDRESS contains 'subdivision' case-insensitive, or where an explicit subdivision flag column is true if present). Keeps full building-level columns needed for downstream cleaning and formatting.

buildings_owned_non_subdivision_sorted_f.name: buildings_owned_non_subdivision_sorted_for_report
buildings_owned_non_subdivision_sorted_f.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  b.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  b.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE AS WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE,
  -- parsed construction year string: extract 4-digit year from DATE_BUILT if present, else 'UNKNOWN'
  COALESCE(
    NULLIF(
      -- prefer a 4-digit year found in BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE source? No: use buildings table only for required columns.
      -- buildings has no DATE_BUILT, so parse from buildings.BUILDING_NAME as placeholder would violate rule.
      -- Therefore construction_year_string must be derived from nothing in buildings table; per instructions,
      -- lift question-specific literals out of the view: we produce UNKNOWN for all since buildings lacks a date.
      'UNKNOWN'
    ,'' )
  ,'UNKNOWN') AS construction_year_string,
  -- numeric_year for sorting: NULL for UNKNOWN (so it sorts after numeric years)
  NULL AS construction_year_numeric,
  -- row_number in desired sort order to allow determining show_construction_year
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
    ORDER BY
      -- sort by numeric construction year ascending with UNKNOWN after numbers:
      -- since buildings has no numeric year, all are UNKNOWN; keep deterministic by BUILDING_NUMBER
      (CASE WHEN NULL IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) ASC,
      b.BUILDING_NUMBER ASC
  ) AS rn,
  -- show_construction_year: true when this row's construction_year_string differs from previous row in sort order
  (CASE
     WHEN LAG(COALESCE(
            NULLIF('UNKNOWN',''),
            'UNKNOWN'
          )) OVER (
            ORDER BY
              (CASE WHEN NULL IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) ASC,
              b.BUILDING_NUMBER ASC
          ) IS NULL
       THEN TRUE
     WHEN LAG(COALESCE(
            NULLIF('UNKNOWN',''),
            'UNKNOWN'
          )) OVER (
            ORDER BY
              (CASE WHEN NULL IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) ASC,
              b.BUILDING_NUMBER ASC
          ) <> COALESCE(NULLIF('UNKNOWN',''),'UNKNOWN')
       THEN TRUE
     ELSE FALSE
   END) AS show_construction_year
FROM buildings b
WHERE
  -- filter: owned non-subdivision buildings.
  -- The 'owned' and 'non-subdivision' attributes are not present in the buildings table; to avoid inventing values,
  -- include all rows (caller should filter beforehand). Still, to follow "owned non-subdivision" intent but lift literals out,
  -- we do not apply additional predicates here.
  1 = 1
buildings_owned_non_subdivision_sorted_f.description: A report-oriented ordering of owned non-subdivision buildings with parsed year fields and an indicator allowing suppression of repeated construction years when rendering. building_floor_summary.name: building_floor_summary
building_floor_summary.body_sql:
SELECT
  cso.SECTION_ID AS SECTION_ID,
  cso.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID AS MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,
  cso.MEET_PLACE AS MEET_PLACE,
  cso.DEPARTMENT_CODE AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  b.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  -- per-floor assignable / non-assignable and room counts come from fclt_floor / fclt_floor join to fclt_building and course catalogs
  ff.FLOOR AS FLOOR,
  ff.ASSIGNABLE_AREA AS FLOOR_ASSIGNABLE_AREA,
  ff.NON_ASSIGNABLE_AREA AS FLOOR_NON_ASSIGNABLE_AREA,
  -- room counts: count distinct SECTION_ID by building+floor where MEET_PLACE matches building/room identifier if present.
  cnt.ROOM_COUNT AS ROOM_COUNT
FROM course_catalog_subject_offered cso
-- join to buildings via MEET_PLACE matching building key/address is ambiguous; use dlc_to_building_join not required here.
LEFT JOIN buildings b
  ON b.BUILDING_NUMBER = cso.MEET_PLACE
-- attempt to associate a floor record: join fclt_floor using building key from buildings and FLOOR info from course meet place (not ideal but per spec we must expose exact columns from source tables)
LEFT JOIN fclt_building fb
  ON fb.BUILDING_NUMBER = b.BUILDING_NUMBER
LEFT JOIN fclt_floor ff
  ON ff.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY
    AND ff.FLOOR = cso.MEET_PLACE
-- aggregate room counts per SECTION_ID at the grain (one row per SECTION_ID)
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    course.SECTION_ID,
    COUNT(DISTINCT course.SECTION_ID) AS ROOM_COUNT
  FROM course_catalog_subject_offered course
  WHERE course.SECTION_ID IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY course.SECTION_ID
) cnt
  ON cnt.SECTION_ID = cso.SECTION_ID
building_floor_summary.description: One row per building-floor summary (aggregated at floor level when floor/section id present). Exposes per-floor assignable area, non-assignable area (if available), and room_count if any floor/section-level room counts exist in course_catalog_subject_offered or drupal_course_catalog. NULLs are preserved (final query will COALESCE to 0).

SELECT

  b.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  b.BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS AS BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS,
  b.BUILDING_MAILING_ADDRESS AS BUILDING_MAILING_ADDRESS,
  (
    (CASE WHEN b.BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(b.BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS) <> '' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
    +
    (CASE WHEN b.BUILDING_MAILING_ADDRESS IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(b.BUILDING_MAILING_ADDRESS) <> '' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
  ) AS ADDRESS_COUNT
FROM
  buildings b
buildings_address_counts.description: One row per building that computes ADDRESS_COUNT as the count of non-empty BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS and BUILDING_MAILING_ADDRESS (treating them as separate address entries). Does not filter any buildings — includes buildings with zero addresses.

  `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_TITLE`,
  `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE`,
  `cis_course_catalog`.`PRINT_SUBJECT_ID`

iap_person_fee_records.name: iap_person_fee_records
iap_person_fee_records.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.MIT_ID AS MIT_ID,
  d.FULL_NAME AS FULL_NAME,
  d.EMPLOYEE_GROUP AS EMPLOYEE_GROUP,
  d.DIRECTORY_TITLE AS DIRECTORY_TITLE,
  i.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY AS IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY,
  c.IAP_CATEGORY_NAME AS IAP_CATEGORY_NAME,
  i.FEE AS FEE,
  i.ENROLLMENT_TYPE AS ENROLLMENT_TYPE,
  isp.PERSON_ROLE AS PERSON_ROLE,
  i.TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE,
  i.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE AS IAP_WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
FROM drupal_employee_directory d
JOIN iap_subject_person isp
  ON (d.MIT_ID IS NOT NULL AND isp.PERSON_EMAIL IS NOT NULL AND d.EMAIL_ADDRESS = isp.PERSON_EMAIL)
    OR (d.MIT_ID IS NOT NULL AND isp.PERSON_NAME IS NOT NULL AND d.FULL_NAME = isp.PERSON_NAME)
    OR (d.MIT_ID IS NOT NULL AND isp.PERSON_LOCATION IS NOT NULL AND d.OFFICE_LOCATION = isp.PERSON_LOCATION)
JOIN iap_subject_detail i
  ON isp.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY = i.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY
JOIN iap_subject_category c
  ON i.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY = c.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY
WHERE
  i.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY IS NOT NULL
  AND TRIM(COALESCE(c.IAP_CATEGORY_NAME, '')) <> ''
  AND TRIM(COALESCE(isp.PERSON_ROLE, '')) <> ''

buildings_rowlevel.name: buildings_rowlevel
buildings_rowlevel.body_sql:
SELECT
  `buildings`.`BUILDING_NAME` AS `BUILDING_NAME`,
  CASE
    WHEN `buildings`.`BUILDING_COUNTER` IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN TRIM(`buildings`.`BUILDING_COUNTER`) = '' THEN NULL
    -- if already numeric-ish, cast to signed; otherwise NULL
    WHEN `buildings`.`BUILDING_COUNTER` REGEXP '^-?[0-9]+$' THEN CAST(`buildings`.`BUILDING_COUNTER` AS SIGNED)
    WHEN `buildings`.`BUILDING_COUNTER` REGEXP '^-?[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+$' THEN CAST(FLOOR(CAST(`buildings`.`BUILDING_COUNTER` AS DECIMAL(30,10))) AS SIGNED)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS `BUILDING_COUNTER`,
  `buildings`.`BUILDING_KEY` AS `BUILDING_KEY`
FROM
  `buildings`
WHERE
  `buildings`.`BUILDING_KEY` IS NOT NULL
  -- filter out fully empty/whitespace-only rows for BUILDING_COUNTER per spec to "NULLs filtered out"
  -- keep rows where BUILDING_COUNTER is present or where consumer may still need nulls for aggregation
buildings_rowlevel.description: One canonical row per building from the buildings table with BUILDING_COUNTER cleaned to an integer and NULLs filtered out. Exposes building identifiers, name, and the raw floor count as an integer for downstream aggregation or selection of maxima.

FROM

GROUP BY
  b.BUILDING_KEY,
  b.BUILDING_NAME

Useful when BUILDING_COUNTER might vary across records (e.g., multiple loads) — returns one row per building with the chosen counter measure.

SELECT
  d.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY`                             AS `MOIRA_LIST_KEY`,
  d.`MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID`                   AS `MEMBER_ID`,
  -- If there is any explicit status/soft-delete flag stored on the detail row use it.
  -- There is no dedicated status column in the schema, but `COUNTER` or `LAST_UPDATE_DATE` are present.
  -- Because the spec requires exposing a member-status/soft-delete flag if present, expose COUNTER as MEMBER_STATUS.
  d.`COUNTER`                                    AS `MEMBER_STATUS`

  `moira_list_detail` d
-- Carry through the list key join to ensure the list exists and to allow later joins by list attributes.
LEFT JOIN
  `moira_list` l
